summary: Per-entity multi-dashboard model + non-removable Overview default (cinatra#700, epic #699). The three new dashboards columns (entity_type, entity_id, is_default) and the partial indexes are ADDITIVE and land in the bootstrap DDL (buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in src/lib/drizzle-store.ts); this migration owns the TRANSFORMATIONAL one-time coexistence backfill that absorbs each existing operator-authored single-id row (system-<surface>:<org>:<user>, surface in agents/artifacts/personal/projects/teams/organizations) as that entity's Overview: entity_type=<surface>, entity_id=organization_id, is_default=true, name='Overview'. Each legacy row maps 1:1 to exactly one Overview (no orphaning, no double-rendering). FAIL-CLOSED: only exact known prefixes AND operator-authored rows (extension_id NULL, is_template false, project_id NULL) are mapped; everything else keeps entity_type NULL and is excluded. IDEMPOTENT (entity_type IS NULL guard → re-run touches zero rows). Gate class destructive: the same PR adds two partial UNIQUE indexes on the existing dashboards table (dashboards_entity_default_uniq, dashboards_entity_name_uniq) — the gate's unique-index-on-existing-table rule — even though those partial indexes cover zero existing rows at creation (entity_type is a brand-new all-NULL column) and the backfill's 1:1 mapping cannot produce a duplicate. Boot order guarantees safety: the bootstrap runs BEFORE core migrations, so the unique indexes already exist and enforce as this UPDATE commits; on a fresh schema the migration is ledger-faked and the table is empty. down() is a NO-OP (a migrated Overview is indistinguishable from a native Overview created later by ensureOverview, so nulling the identity fields would corrupt native rows; the ledger records the run). SEQ: assigned at merge; shipped max is 0047. A concurrent W5 lane (#1617) claimed 0048, so this migration was renumbered 0048→0049 at merge-prep (0049 > 0047 shipped max; gaps are tolerated) — renumber-at-merge is normal.
